title: From Hourly to Annual: How to Calculate a League Salary in Australia
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary using 38-hour weeks, including National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, super, and tax.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is the hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual salary calculation?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. When calculating annual salary for a casual, you should first add the 25% loading to the base rate, then multiply by hours per week and 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage base rate of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides that show the correct loaded rates for each award.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the annual salary figure?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your annual salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. If your annual gross pay is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund. This is not part of your take-home pay and is not subject to income tax at your marginal rate.

faqs.q: What tax will I pay on my annual salary in 2026–27?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% on $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. The tax-free threshold is included. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate your net income after tax and Medicare.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly-to-Annual Conversion

Whether you're negotiating a new job offer or comparing a league salary against the National Minimum Wage, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual figure is essential. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Commission. The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a part-time or casual worker, the same formula applies using your typical weekly hours.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38-hour week is the benchmark for full-time employment under the National Employment Standards. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) is set on this basis. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the formula accordingly.

### From Weekly to Fortnightly

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, at the National Minimum Wage, a fortnightly gross is $2,009.80. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers quoted per fortnight.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most industries have specific awards that set higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, detailing classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates. For instance, the Health Services Award and the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Award have recently updated rates. Always check the correct award for your job.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. When calculating annual salary for a casual, apply the loading first. The Fair Work Commission states that the casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour. If you are using our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, enter the base rate and select the casual loading checkbox to get the correct loaded rate.

## Including Superannuation

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund. This is not included in your take-home pay. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross salary is before tax. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on $18,201–$45,000
- 30% on $45,001–$135,000
- 37% on $135,001–$190,000
- 45% above $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator to estimate your net income after tax and Medicare. Note that HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included in this basic estimate.

## Example: Comparing a League Salary

Suppose you are considering a job offer with an hourly rate of $50. To find the annual gross salary: $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. This is a league salary well above the minimum. Your fortnightly gross would be $3,800. After tax (using the 2026–27 rates) and Medicare, your estimated take-home pay would be around $74,000 per year, depending on your circumstances. Super of 12% adds $11,856 on top.

### Award vs Enterprise Agreement

If your employer has an enterprise agreement, it may set different rates. Pay guides from the Fair Work Ombudsman do not apply if you are covered by an agreement. Always check your employment contract and the applicable industrial instrument.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For precise calculations tailored to your situation, refer to the [reference tables](/data) or consult a qualified accountant.
